requirement:
A successful `InspectionContext::read` records the node's identity and the
fingerprint of the returned contents, under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs`. A failed read records no
successful observation. The evidence becomes stale when a later read of that
node has a different fingerprint; a failure to resolve it is reported by
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records`.

The SDK prepares the contents and their fingerprint together and records
the observation when those contents are delivered. The dependency describes
the supplied contents, rather than a replacement read.
rationale:
I judge the marked tests adequate for `requirements.sdk.graph.context-tools.read_node.inputs`. I did not request any implementation source.

I read the supplied test sources and checked them against each obligation. The obligations that `read_node.inputs` delegates to the cited `requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs` and `checking_records` need no separate test here.

**Obligations and the tests that cover them**

- **A successful read records node identity and the fingerprint of the returned contents.**
  - `tests/validation.rs#fn[direct_reads_return_complete_unicode_contents_and_snapshots]` reads node 1 with `InspectionContext::read` and `read_snapshot`. It asserts `dependencies() == [Dependency::Node(1, fp(original))]`. It covers an empty string and a large multi-byte Unicode string.
  - `agent/tests.rs#fn[graph_tools_record_delivered_snapshots_and_prepared_pages_do_not_record_delivery]` covers the model `read_node` tool path. It asserts a `Dependency::Node(Node(2), fingerprint)` whose value is the full 18,000-character contents. The finished record's dependencies equal the observations.
  - `agent/tests.rs#fn[concurrent_tool_agents_isolate_histories_pages_and_submissions_and_share_reads]` checks the recorded `Dependency::Node` entries for nodes 1 and 2 with the "content" scheme. It also checks that the finished record carries the same dependencies.

- **A failed read records no successful observation.**
  - In `direct_reads_return_complete_unicode_contents_and_snapshots`, reading a missing node 9 returns an error and `dependencies()` stays empty.
  - In `snapshots_record_exact_reads_and_retain_distinct_versions`, a failed `read(&2)` adds nothing to the dependency list.
  - In `agent/tests.rs#fn[node_preparation_tool_errors_allow_recovery_without_recording_undelivered_contents]`, the contents formatter fails while the node is being prepared. The test asserts the error reaches the agent as a tool-result error and that no dependencies are recorded.
  - In `graph_tools_record_delivered_snapshots_and_prepared_pages_do_not_record_delivery`, a `read_node` call whose result is never delivered, because the next completion fails, leaves the dependencies empty. The same test shows that a read delivered through `contents_of_current_node` is recorded.

- **The evidence becomes stale when a later read has a different fingerprint.**
  - `snapshots_record_exact_reads_and_retain_distinct_versions` reads "before", changes the node, then reads "after". It asserts both observations are preserved in order and that the finished record is not current (`!record_is_current(...)`).
  - `direct_reads_return_complete_unicode_contents_and_snapshots` also asserts that a record is not current after the contents are replaced.

- **Contents and fingerprint are prepared together, the observation is recorded on delivery, and the dependency describes the supplied contents rather than a replacement read.**
  - `agent/tests.rs#fn[graph_read_pages_retain_the_prepared_snapshot_after_contents_change]` changes the node contents between the `read_node` call and the page request. It asserts the node was read only once, the recorded fingerprint equals the original contents, and the delivered page contains the original text and not the replacement.
  - `direct_reads_return_complete_unicode_contents_and_snapshots` asserts the returned contents and snapshot still format as the original after the graph changes. Its recorded fingerprint is the original's.
  - The prepared-but-undelivered cases above cover "records when delivered".

- **Failure to resolve is reported by `checking_records`.** This is cited context, so it needs no test here.

I found no plausible requirement-violating behavior that these assertions would accept. For example, fingerprinting a re-read, recording on a failed or undelivered read, or collapsing differing fingerprints would each fail one of the assertions above. All the tests carry `{test}` references to the subject, so there are no marking gaps.

fingerprint of the returned contents, under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs`. A failed read records no
successful observation. The evidence becomes stale when a later read of that
node has a different fingerprint; a failure to resolve it is reported by
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records`.
The SDK prepares the contents and their fingerprint together and records
the observation when those contents are delivered. The dependency describes
the supplied contents, rather than a replacement read.
:::{req} node_inputs
Finishing a verification includes every successful tracked node read in its
`Fingerprinted`, whether ordinary code or a model tool requested it. Each observation
contains the node identity and the fingerprint of the contents actually supplied.
A failed read returns an error without inventing a successful observation.
Repeating an identical observation adds no information. Reading the same
identity with two different fingerprints preserves both observations.
:::{req} checking_records
```rust,ignore
// Method on Validator<D>.
/// Compare each recorded input with the current domain state.
/// Return true when every fingerprint still matches, including an empty trace.
pub fn check_inputs<O>(
&self,
inputs: &Fingerprinted<D, O>,
) -> Result<bool, D::Error>;
The method resolves the recorded dependencies through graph operations and
fingerprinting, comparing each with its saved observation. A fingerprint
mismatch returns `Ok(false)` and permits an early return; it need not resolve
later dependencies. An encountered dependency-resolution failure returns an
error.
The method observes the current state that the caller intends to inspect.
Freshness checking has a separate observation scope from criterion execution.
Checked observations enter the new trace when execution explicitly reads
or delivers them.
A checked snapshot can be reused if it still represents the current state.
